title: Track count per genre
prompt_md:
Using the **Track** and **Genre** tables in the Chinook database, count how many tracks belong to each genre.

Return exactly two columns:
- `Name` — the genre's name
- `TrackCount` — the number of tracks in that genre

Sort by `TrackCount` **descending**, then by `Name` **ascending** to break ties.
starter_code:
SELECT
  -- g.Name AS Name,
  -- COUNT(*) AS TrackCount
FROM Track t
JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
-- GROUP BY ...
-- ORDER BY ...;
hints: Join Track to Genre on GenreId so each track carries its genre name.
GROUP BY the genre, COUNT(*) the tracks, and add Name as a secondary sort key for deterministic ties.
explanation_md: Inner-join `Track` to `Genre` on `GenreId`, group by the genre, and `COUNT(*)` the rows in each group. Sorting by count descending with `Name` ascending gives a deterministic order.
solution_sql: SELECT g.Name AS Name, COUNT(*) AS TrackCount FROM Track t JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId GROUP BY g.GenreId ORDER BY TrackCount DESC, Name ASC;

title: Five longest tracks
prompt_md:
From the **Track** table, find the five longest tracks by duration.

Return exactly two columns:
- `Name` — the track name
- `Milliseconds` — its duration in milliseconds

Sort by `Milliseconds` **descending**, breaking ties by `Name` **ascending**, and return only the top 5 rows.
starter_code:
SELECT Name, Milliseconds
FROM Track
-- ORDER BY ...
-- LIMIT ...;
hints: ORDER BY Milliseconds DESC puts the longest first.
Use LIMIT 5, and add Name ASC as a tie-breaker so the order is stable.
explanation_md: Order the tracks by `Milliseconds` descending (with `Name` as a deterministic tie-breaker) and keep only the first five rows with `LIMIT 5`.
solution_sql: SELECT Name, Milliseconds FROM Track ORDER BY Milliseconds DESC, Name ASC LIMIT 5;

title: Invoices per billing country
prompt_md:
Using the **Invoice** table, count how many invoices were billed to each country.

Return exactly two columns:
- `Country` — the value of `BillingCountry`
- `InvoiceCount` — the number of invoices billed to that country

Sort by `InvoiceCount` **descending**, then by `Country` **ascending** to break ties.
starter_code:
SELECT
  -- BillingCountry AS Country,
  -- COUNT(*) AS InvoiceCount
FROM Invoice
-- GROUP BY ...
-- ORDER BY ...;
hints: GROUP BY BillingCountry and COUNT(*) to tally invoices per country.
Add Country as a secondary ascending sort key for a deterministic order.
explanation_md: Group invoices by `BillingCountry` and `COUNT(*)` per group. Sort by the count descending with `Country` ascending as a tie-breaker.
solution_sql: SELECT BillingCountry AS Country, COUNT(*) AS InvoiceCount FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY InvoiceCount DESC, Country ASC;

title: Total spend per customer
prompt_md:
The finance team wants each customer's lifetime spend. Join **Customer** to **Invoice** and sum each customer's invoice totals.

Return exactly two columns:
- `Customer` — the customer's full name as `FirstName || ' ' || LastName`
- `TotalSpent` — the sum of that customer's `Invoice.Total`, rounded to 2 decimals

Sort by `TotalSpent` **descending**, then by `Customer` **ascending**. Only include customers who have at least one invoice.
starter_code:
SELECT
  c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS Customer,
  -- ROUND(SUM(...), 2) AS TotalSpent
FROM Customer c
JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
-- GROUP BY ...
-- ORDER BY ...;
hints: An inner join to Invoice naturally drops customers with no invoices.
Concatenate the name with || , SUM(i.Total), and ROUND(..., 2).
explanation_md: Inner-join `Customer` to `Invoice` (which drops customers with no invoices), group by the customer, and `SUM(Total)` rounded to two decimals. Concatenate the name for the label.
solution_sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS Customer, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS TotalSpent FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC, Customer ASC;

title: Artists with two or more albums
prompt_md:
Using the **Album** and **Artist** tables, find every artist who has released **at least two** albums.

Return exactly two columns:
- `Name` — the artist's name
- `AlbumCount` — how many albums they have

Sort by `AlbumCount` **descending**, then by `Name` **ascending**.
starter_code:
SELECT
  ar.Name AS Name,
  COUNT(*) AS AlbumCount
FROM Album al
JOIN Artist ar ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
-- GROUP BY ...
-- HAVING ...
-- ORDER BY ...;
hints: Filtering on COUNT(*) needs HAVING, not WHERE.
GROUP BY the artist and keep groups where COUNT(*) >= 2.
explanation_md: Join `Album` to `Artist`, group by the artist, and keep only groups whose `COUNT(*) >= 2` using `HAVING` (you can't filter an aggregate in `WHERE`).
solution_sql: SELECT ar.Name AS Name, COUNT(*) AS AlbumCount FROM Album al JOIN Artist ar ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY AlbumCount DESC, Name ASC;
